Each of these premium paint finishes costs an additional $595.

Of note, destination charges didn’t increase for the 2027 model year, still at $1,315 for most US states. Taxes, title and other applicable fees are also extra, while individual dealers determine actual transaction prices.

#4496. Lexus is taking a page from China for its next electric SUV launching in 2027

Toyota’s luxury brand Lexus is launching a new electric SUV in 2027, its first vehicle built in China in over two decades.

It’s official. Toyota is breaking from tradition, planning to develop and produce the new vehicle in China rather than its home market of Japan.

Lexus confirmed the new vehicle will be made at its new manufacturing plant in Jinshan, Shanghai, and will go on sale in 2027.

As the first Lexus factory built from scratch overseas, the company said the new plant will bring together its global manufacturing capabilities.

Toyota broke ground on the facility in June 2025, saying the new facility will unlock “Lexus speed” as it aims to keep pace with domestic brands like BYD. Construction was expected to be completed this past August, with the first vehicle scheduled to roll off the assembly line in the fall of 2027.

The first Lexus model will be an electric SUV, produced using advanced manufacturing methods such as gigacasting to reduce costs and speed up output.

The facility will be a cornerstone of Toyota’s comeback plans in China, where it’s struggled to compete with local brands.

Production capacity will be around 1,000 units per month in 2027 as Toyota ramps up to “tens of thousands” in 2028.

Toyota’s sales plunged nearly 20% in China last month, marking its eighth consecutive month with lower sales than the year prior. The market in China “remained weak due in part to rising gasoline prices, while the market for gasoline vehicles and hybrid vehicles was particularly affected,” Toyota said.

In the first nine months of 2026, Toyota sold just over 1.05 million vehicles in China, 18.9% fewer than in the same period last year.

Lexus’ new Shanghai facility is wholly owned by Toyota, enabling it to produce vehicles in China through its joint ventures.

The new electric SUV will go on sale in China in 2027. Specific details, including battery, range, and prices, have yet to be announced.

As part of its “with China, for China, strategy, Lexus said it will “continue to use China as a source of innovation,” adding it will “deepen localization efforts” to bring classic models to the market that meet local needs.

Toyota joins the growing list of major OEMs that are already tapping, or plan to tap, China for its next-generation electric vehicles.

While in other global markets, Toyota is sticking to its “multi-pathway” strategy, which includes all powertrains from electric to ICE; in China, it’s being forced to adapt.

China is Toyota’s third-largest market, following the US and Japan. To stay competitive and turn things around in China, Toyota will rely more on local partners and suppliers.

Developing the new Lexus electric SUV in China first rather than Japan is significant given Toyota’s traditional ways.

Typically, it takes Toyota about four to five years to fully develop a new vehicle. In China, automakers are now building them in as little as two years.

Toyota, like many automakers at this point, is turning to China for new tech, batteries, production methods, and other EV components to keep pace.

General Motors is boosting the long-haul capability of its upcoming half-ton trucks. When the redesigned 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and GMC Sierra 1500 arrive, models equipped with the popular 3.0-liter Duramax diesel will feature a significantly larger Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) tank. This upgrade marks a major shift for the upcoming truck platform as GM pushes to improve towing efficiency and cross-country range.

The larger DEF tank pairs directly with the new 34-gallon extended-range fuel tanks arriving across the half-ton lineup. For drivers who rely on the Duramax for heavy towing, this means stretching the distance between mandatory fill-ups and minimizing service visits for routine maintenance. This diesel upgrade arrives alongside sweeping changes to the broader engine lineup, which will also introduce larger displacement options and heftier price tags for traditional gasoline buyers.

According to a recent report from GM Authority, GM fitting these larger fluid reservoirs forces a tough design trade-off. To squeeze both the bigger DEF and the massive 34-gallon fuel tank beneath the floorboards, engineers had to completely eliminate the rear under-seat storage bins. For years, owners have relied on these hidden compartments to securely stash expensive tools, emergency gear, and everyday items.

Losing this built-in utility confirms earlier reports that the redesigned trucks would suffer from shrinking cabin volume compared to the outgoing 2026 models. Moving forward, 2027 Silverado and Sierra owners will need to adapt. Drivers will have to depend on the redesigned front center console, stick to the standard gloveboxes, or purchase lockable aftermarket bed boxes to keep their valuables out of sight.

GM is making the right call for its core truck buyers. Customers who spend extra money on the 3.0-liter Duramax diesel care more about uninterrupted highway range and towing convenience than saving a few cubic inches of cab storage. The ability to pull heavy trailers for much longer distances without frantically hunting down a truck stop DEF pump is a massive win for both fleet operators and private owners.

While giving up the rear under-seat storage is definitely frustrating for everyday family utility, the extra fluid capacity ultimately makes the Silverado and Sierra much better workhorses. When weighed against the massive towing and range improvements arriving for the next production cycle, losing a couple of plastic storage bins is a perfectly acceptable trade-off for serious truck owners.

#4493. BYD sold more EVs last month than the US did all quarter, topping 300,000

BYD sold over 300,000 electric vehicles in October, a new record and more than the US managed in the entire third quarter.

The world’s leading EV maker is showing no signs of slowing down. BYD sold 490,168 new energy vehicles (NEVs) in October, up 11% from the prior year and the company’s highest monthly total in 2026.

BYD’s battery electric vehicles drove the growth, with a record 305,743 units sold, up 37% year over year and marking the first time its EV sales have crossed the 300,000 mark.

To put that into perspective, just over 262,500 EVs were sold in the US in the entire third quarter combined, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates.

October marked BYD’s sixth straight month of higher sales growth and its third straight month of higher EV sales. Through October, BYD sold 1,953,700 electric vehicles, up 6% from the same period last year.

BYD’s all-electric vehicles (EVs) accounted for about 63% of total sales last month. Plug-in hybrid vehicles, meanwhile, fell 17% in October to 177,382 units. Through October, BYD’s PHEV sales fell 11% to 1,625,969 units.

According to BYD’s filing, the company exported 170,194 vehicles in October as it expands overseas to drive growth in markets like Europe, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America.

Through October, BYD exported over 1.5 million electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, nearly double compared to last year.

By the end of 2026, BYD expects overseas shipments to reach about 2 million vehicles. In 2027, that number is expected to rise to more than 2.5 million vehicles.

#4492. 8 Elden Ring Details That Suggest Some of the Biggest Mysteries Still Aren’t Solved

Melissa Sarnowski is a Gaming Writer at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2022. She specializes in lists, reviews, and features, with additional experience writing guides for Hardcore Gamer. Before joining DualShockers, Melissa contributed to Screen Rant, and she currently writes for CBR and

Elden Ring is weird, and I mean that in the best way. FromSoftware builds elaborate worlds in each game the developers make, and the effort and attention to detail that goes into those worlds mean that you can spend dozens of hours digging into the lore and still not have a clear idea of it.

Bored with the way you go about your journey in The Lands Between? Here are the 10 best ways to make your second Elden Ring playthrough different.

This design for lore also means that you likely won't find an answer to every question. If you're like me, then the mystery is part of the charm. It keeps you wondering, and that keeps you playing as you search for answers that might not fully exist in-game in as straightforward of a way as you’d wish.

My favorite mystery is the Gloam-Eyed Queen. You never get to see her, but multiple items refer to her, and you learn that she was the main rival of Marika. It's also heavily implied that she still has some followers in the Lands Between.

However, we don't know her real identity, what happened to her, or where she is if she's alive. One interesting theory is that Melina is the Gloam-Eyed Queen due to her one eye seeming sealed shut, but when it's open in the Frenzied Flame ending, it has a gloam color to it.

This is a bit interesting because we know why the Land of Shadow was separated from the Lands Between. Marika effectively sealed away her past in the Land of Shadow, but more importantly, she was able to block access to the exact gate that let her ascend to godhood. Of course, she would put measures in place that prevented others from getting power like that.

The mystery is how she separated it and how Miquella was able to create an entrance that others could follow him through. However, the methods aren't exactly important enough to impact the lore much, and we just don't know the extent of Marika’s abilities.

Aside from its name, there are multiple mentions of locations beyond the Lands Between. We also know that the Tarnished, when they had their Grace removed by Marika, were sent away and returned later. So, that means that the Lands Between is a place that can be accessed from other lands.

It also raises the question as to why the Lands Between is so unique and has the Erdtree and, previously, the Crucible. Are the other lands not worth the attention of the Outer Gods, or is it just that the gods we know of aren't interested, but others might be? There's just not enough information to find an answer.

The Greater Will is well-known, and a few gods like the God of Rot, Formless Mother, and Frenzied Flame are mentioned enough that we know they exist and have some interest in the Lands Between. However, we really don't know much about the gods or what they want from this land.

These Elden Ring bosses are underrated and deserve more praise.

It's obvious that the Erdtree is what they're after, but the Erdtree is almost certainly built on the Crucible, which could be another goal or the main goal. But the Greater Will apparently has the ability to create and defeat gods, so it seems strange that it would want power from the Lands Between unless it's to keep it out of the hands of other gods.

Nokstella alone is filled with so much mystery that it's difficult to condense into a summary when you need a ton of context and explanations. Honestly, you could write a novella on the many unanswered questions that come from this location.

The Nox, who built Nokstella after rebelling against the Greater Will unsuccessfully, were originally thought to be connected to the Numen and Marika, but the DLC puts Marika in a completely different location. But then you have the connections between the Black Knives and Marika, along with the Black Knives being connected to the Nox. There are too many threads and almost no answers here.

Placidusax has two heads when you encounter him for his boss fight, but he also has a few stumps where more heads once were. The story is that his missing heads were cut off by Bayle, and you can find that two of his heads are with Bayle when you see him in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC.

Except that's not accounting for every head. Placidusax has two remaining. Bayle has two of the missing ones, but if you look at Placidusax’s model and the Old Lord's Talisman, it shows that he should have five heads. The problem is that we have no idea what happened to the fifth one.

There are seven walking mausoleums in Elden Ring, and we can assume that they were made by the Nox because of their design, which matches the buildings in Nokstella, a style found nowhere else. The interesting part is that we're told they house soulless demigods, so those in the same state as Godwyn.

If that's true, then the bodies in them must be Marika’s children. A ghost even tells you when talking about one that it has Marika's unwanted child in it. When you start Elden Ring, you feel like you know who Marika's children are, but the details of the world let you know that she apparently had far more children than you think as you dig into the lore.

I'm fascinated by the Gate of Divinity, and I think it's one of the most well-known mysteries if you played the DLC or even watched the trailer for it. This is where Marika ascended to godhood, and Miquella later followed in her footsteps, albeit with a much shorter reign since you end it immediately.

Yet we know nothing about this gate other than the fact that it grants divinity. There seem to be requirements for being able to use it successfully, but beyond that we don't know how or why it works. We don't even know where it connects to.

FromSoftware makes such fascinating games that leave you thinking about them even years after they were released, encouraging you to explore every bit of content. Unfortunately, like most of their games, we're probably not going to get answers for every mystery in Elden Ring.

FromSoftware games are full of many NPCs, but many of them are hurt by your intervention, and not helped. Here are the best/saddest examples.

The 2022 action RPG by From Software joins the Souls-like subgenre by presenting one of the most punishing games in the field with grotesque, memorable bosses to keep you up at night. Inside a world built by Hidetaka Miyazaki and Game of Thrones writer George R.R. Martin, Elden Ring's gothic landscape, unforgiving combat, and top-tier exploration will keep you invested well into the year.

The Ford Ranger Raptor is the horsepower king among gas-powered midsize pickups, at least on paper, with its 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged EcoBoost V6 producing 405 horsepower. That exceeds the 326-hp output of the 2.4-liter i-Force Max turbo hybrid powertrain in the Toyota Tacoma, America’s best-selling midsize pickup. The Nissan Frontier takes a different approach with its naturally aspirated 3.8-liter V6, but the automaker is apparently exploring a more powerful formula.

At this year’s SEMA Show, Nissan has brought a new Frontier-based concept called the Ronin, which adopts twin-turbocharging hardware from one of the brand’s most iconic nameplates, the GT-R. Both may have the same displacement, but the truck retains its VQ38DD engine rather than swapping in the GT-R’s VR38DETT V6. The automaker didn’t say how much the forced induction boosted its output, but for reference, the regular model already makes 310 horsepower.

This concept is particularly noteworthy given that the production Frontier makes 310 horsepower across the lineup, including the off-road-focused Pro-4X. Some may argue that this is more than enough, even for off-road driving, while others may see the single-engine lineup as limiting its appeal, especially compared with the Ford Ranger, which offers multiple engine options.

Nissan paired the GT-R-derived turbocharging system with EcuTek engine management, a custom front-mounted intercooler, dual off-road air intakes, and a Nismo Off Road exhaust. The suspension also received extensive upgrades, including modified Titan components, a rear axle swap, Bilstein Black Hawk shocks, and custom racing control arms. CJD Racing’s long-travel suspension components provide a four-inch lift, a 12-inch wider track, and 14 inches of suspension travel.

Other notable modifications include a custom front fascia, grille, and bumpers; prototype Nismo Off Road fender flares and running lights; Nismo Off Road 6-inch driving lights, 4-inch A-pillar lights, rock sliders, and all-weather floor mats; custom Kinetic sport bucket seats; and a dashboard gauge pod displaying boost, oil pressure, and exhaust temperature.

As a concept truck, the Frontier Ronin has no confirmed production plans, though Nissan can gather feedback that could influence future products. The automaker cites the Rock Creek lineup as an example of how previous SEMA concepts have inspired production models. So, with enough interest, the Japanese marque might consider adding a new, more powerful trim above the Pro-4X, potentially matching or even exceeding the Ranger Raptor’s horsepower on paper.

Nissan has already collaborated with Roush Performance to build a more extreme version of the Frontier called the Pro-4X R, featuring upgrades such as a two-inch suspension lift, Öhlins 2.0 off-road shocks, and 17-inch titanium-finished wheels. However, it retains the standard powertrain.

Aside from the Frontier Ronin, the automaker has brought two other concepts to the 2026 SEMA Show: the Pathfinder XE-V6 Concept, which celebrates the model’s 40th anniversary, and the Armada Jungle Patrol Concept. The event runs from November 3 to 6 at the Las Vegas Convention Center.

#4489. Nissan Turns the Armada into the Safari-Ready Jungle Patrol Concept

The Armada Jungle Patrol loses its roof, rides on a custom long-travel suspension, and wears tubular bumpers and lots of auxiliary lighting.

Each year, the SEMA show in Las Vegas allows automakers to let their creativity shine through custom concepts based on production vehicles. In 2025, Nissan turned its full-size Armada SUV into the desert-ready Dune Patrol, adding a long-travel suspension, unique bumpers, and a durable roof rack. Now, for 2026, Nissan has modified the Armada once again, this time transforming it into the Jungle Patrol, ripping off the roof to make the SUV into the ideal safari companion.

The Armada Jungle Patrol’s biggest change is, obviously, the lack of a roof, with the solid shelter replaced by a tubular roll cage, providing a better view of the natural world you’re exploring. Just be ready to speed away if a lion gets a little too curious about the tasty treats sitting inside. The rear section has been fitted with inward-facing bench seats, a common setup in safari vehicles.

See all results for new 2026 Nissan Armada for sale near ?

Nissan also upgraded the Armada to tackle more serious terrain. The Jungle Patrol rides on prototype 18-inch NISMO wheels wrapped in 37-inch Yokohama Geolandar G003 M/T tires, which are suspended on a custom long-travel setup from CJD Racing. The setup utilizes high-performance adjustable coil-overs with remote reservoirs and bypass, and the Jungle Patrol has a wider track than the regular Armada.

The Jungle Patrol is also equipped with custom steel bumpers and fender flares, and there are NISMO off-road lights mounted on the bumper and roof to illuminate the jungle at night. Nissan caps off the look with a unique livery, which reads “Jungle Patrol” in a scrawled font and features what look like the claw marks of some intimidating jungle beast down the rear doors.

As with the Desert Patrol last year, Nissan has left the standard 425-hp twin-turbo 3.5-liter V-6 engine untouched but added a custom NISMO cat-back exhaust. While the Armada Jungle Patrol is a fun experiment, we assume it will never enter production given its extreme mission, but some features, like the prototype wheels and custom bumpers, could one day be offered as official NISMO aftermarket parts.

Toyota Celica Officially Returns for 2027, But You Can't Buy One

The Best-Selling Hyundai SUV In October Wasn’t The Tucson

Even some of the most popular, highly regarded cars in the world have their quirks. We found out that much with the latest Toyota RAV4, which has a center console design that many owners have found compromises comfort. It turns out that the Honda CR-V, the RAV4’s fiercest rival, has an unusual pain point of its own. The best-selling SUV in the U.S. this year so far, numerous CR-V owners have uncovered flaws in the Honda’s windshield wiper design. One would imagine that getting a wiper design wrong in 2026 is near impossible, but a lot of CR-V owners have been left frustrated by the wiper system’s inability to properly clean the windshield.

There are two separate issues with the CR-V’s wiper design, both of which have been spoken about at length on several social media forums. We also found complaints listed on the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) website.

The first issue involves the placement of the wiper system spray nozzles, which are situated on the wiper arms themselves. Many owners have found that when attempting to clean the windshield, the nozzles only begin spraying water when the wiper blades are roughly halfway up the windshield. As a result, many owners have complained that it’s not possible to properly clean the windshield, particularly in snowy or icy conditions, where hood-mounted nozzles would be more practical and better able to disperse the water.

“I will die on this hill. The wipers (especially when I’m using them w/windshield wiper fluid) are my ONLY gripe about this car. The design is terrible,” said one owner on Reddit.

“Having the windshield wiper fluid come out of the blades rather than spraying directly onto the windshield is useless as the fluid comes out while the wipers are half way up and fluid then gets pushed off the windshield and flows down the driver’s side window again affecting the driver’s visibility,” said another owner of a 2023 CR-V, who is based in Connecticut. This owner shared their experience on the NHTSA’s website.

These wiper-mounted nozzles are meant to eliminate the wind deflection or blind spots created by traditional, hood-mounted nozzles, but it appears that the current CR-V’s nozzles have not been properly engineered.

The second issue involves the driver’s-side wiper, which several owners say does not reach the edge of the windshield on the left. This leaves a significant portion of the windshield covered in dirt, creating another visibility concern. Some owners say the wipers only work properly if the vehicle is in Accessory Mode, while others were told by dealerships that the gap left on the driver’s side is normal.

“While driving my 2025 Hybrid CRV with 4K miles in a light rain, the wiper stopped going all the way to the edge and now only goes 90% of the way up no matter the setting. In a heavy rain, it will go 96%, and in accessory mode it goes up 100% of the way,” said an owner of a 2025 CR-V on Reddit. Other owners in the thread reported the same issue, with many filing complaints with the NHTSA and hoping for a recall. After all, visibility-related safety defects are often considered serious enough to initiate a recall.

A video posted by another Reddit user shows that an unacceptably large portion of the CR-V’s windshield isn’t reached by the left wiper blade, with a few commenters suggesting that it’s a software issue, not a mechanical alignment problem.

How to change wiper blades and washer fluid | Autoblog Wrenched

Manufacturers have invested heavily in technologies that enhance driver visibility, from blind-spot monitoring systems to surround-view monitors and pedestrian detection systems. But all of that doesn’t mean much if one of the most basic safety features, the windshield wiper, doesn’t do its job properly. At the very least, the performance of the current CR-V’s windshield wipers are inconsistent from one model to the next. While no recall has been issued for this condition and windshield wiper testing does not form part of safety tests run by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, that does not mean there isn’t a genuine concern. As visibility impacts overall safety, we would like to see Honda address the concern.

#4487. Toyota’s Corolla Cross EV spotted for the first time [Images]

Toyota is giving its best-selling Corolla a major makeover, and an all-electric version is part of the plan. The upcoming Corolla Cross EV was captured in public for the first time ahead of its expected 2027 debut.

The Corolla has always been “a car for everyone,” Toyota’s former president and current CEO, Koji Sato, said after unveiling the next-gen Corolla Concept at last year’s Japan Mobility Show.

Since it went on sale 60 years ago, over 57 million drivers have chosen the Corolla, making it Toyota’s best-selling vehicle ever.

The Corolla has undergone 12 model changes since 1966, but the compact car is about to undergo its biggest transformation yet.

Although it’s still a top seller, the Corolla has lost some of its appeal as new, more advanced, and efficient options have emerged. Toyota looks to change that with the next-generation model.

It will remain “a car for everyone,” as Sato said, but the next-gen Corolla will come in multiple powertrains, including an all-electric version.

“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle―whatever the power source―let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive,” Sato said at the Japan Mobility Show last October.

Ahead of its expected debut sometime in 2027, a disguised Corolla Cross EV was spotted driving near Toyota’s European headquarters and R&D center.

New images from Chinese media outlet Autohome show what’s expected to be the all-electric Corolla Cross, with a closed-off grille and a unique body design.

The new Corolla will be the first to use Toyota’s new “multipathway” platform that will support electric, hybrid, gas, and other powertrains.

Toyota hasn’t revealed specifics, including battery or powertrain specs, but the next-gen Corolla EV is expected to remain close in style to the Concept. Aside from the massive COROLLA badge on the back, it looks like an entirely different vehicle with a near sports-car-like silhouette.

In an exclusive interview with Japanese media NHK in July, Toyota’s current chairman and former CEO, Akio Toyoda, warned that the company “cannot survive” if it does not adapt amid new competition and technology from China.

During the special, which went behind the scenes at Toyota’s “top secret” development site, several blurred Corolla Concept body types, including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and GR model, were revealed in the background.

According to a recent Nikkei report, Toyota plans to begin production of the next-gen Corolla in 2028 through its joint venture with Chinese state-owned FAW Group, FAW Toyota Motor.

The Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations with a driving range of at least 250 miles.

Let's hope that Toyota gets the Corolla EV right, because if it offers the right range for the right price but still feels fundamentally like a Corolla it is an EV that would get consideration from buyers who wouldn't otherwise consider an EV.

They're the buyers that trust Toyota and who consider the Corolla to be a nice safe choice for a car. And by safe, that means a vehicle that may not be all that exciting, but also a vehicle that they won't regret buying. Needless to say, these are not people who read Electrek, or even Car & Driver, for that matter. But there's a lot more of them than there are of us.

The hybrid version will reportedly use a new 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.

Toyota has yet to confirm the electric version will launch in the US. According to Car and Driver, the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.

#4486. HoYoverse's Petit Planet Launches in December, Switch 2 Port Coming 2027

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

In the gacha gaming scene, HoYoverse, international division of Chinese game developer miHoYo, has become one of the definitive faces, offering games like the high-grossing Genshin Impact, the stylish Zenless Zone Zero, and my personal favorite gacha game, Honkai: Star Rail. Even as new challengers constantly appear in the gacha scene, and there are a lot of them, HoYo maintains a powerful presence thanks to its games, and especially its character designs.

We were able to get some extensive time with HoYoverse's upcoming life simulator, Petit Planet, and were left grinning from ear-to-ear.

While all of its other games are merrily chugging along, HoYo is still working on even more titles to add to its catalog and appeal to an even larger variety of potential players. One such title is Petit Planet, a life sim game in a similar vein to titles like Animal Crossing. Petit Planet has run several beta tests since its initial announcement in September of last year, and it seems HoYo is finally ready to launch the proverbial rocket.

In a pre-launch special program that aired over the weekend, HoYo officially revealed Petit Planet’s global launch date as December 4, 2026. As is typical for HoYo games, it’ll be launching on PC, both via HoYo’s own HoYoPlay launcher and the Epic Games Store, and mobile devices via Android and iOS. However, in a first for HoYo, the game will also be launching on the Switch 2, albeit in 2027 after the initial launch, as announced today on a post to the game’s official X, formerly Twitter account.

Several of HoYo’s other titles, primarily Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, and Zenless Zone Zero, have been made available on gaming consoles before, with their primary affinity being the PlayStation 4 and, later, PlayStation 5, though Genshin and ZZZ specifically also made it over to the XBOX Series X/S. However, none of the developer’s titles have made it to either the Nintendo Switch or Switch 2, at least until now.

Honkai: Nexus Anima is shaping up to be a stand-out monster taming game from HoYoverse.

The post on the official Petit Planet X that announced the Switch 2 port didn’t specify when, exactly, we’ll be seeing this port beyond a broad window of 2027, but it is still an interesting addition to HoYo’s wheelhouse, and hopefully a sign that its other titles are on the way as well. Maybe we can start getting  more Star Rail crossovers…

None of the developer’s titles have made it to either the Nintendo Switch or Switch 2, at least until now.

Even if you plan on playing the game on the Switch 2, you might want to make your account ahead of time anyway, as due to the large number of pre-registrations the game received during its developmental period, there will be a swath of rewards for all players upon initial log-in. All players will receive 2 Blissful Floral & Fruit Tea, 2 Red Star Fireworks, 2 Sweet Specials, 100 Bazaar Jelly, the Sproutling Outfit, and the Bestie Star Light.

With this latest announcement, it’s shaping up to be quite the winter season for those interested in gacha games. Following Petit Planet’s launch on December 4, an entirely new gacha game, Silver Palace, will be launching a little over a week later on December 14 for PC, PS5, Android, and iOS, as that game’s developers announced a couple of days ago.

NetEase Games and Naked Rain revealed a brand-new trailer for Ananta during ONL's gamescom.

Not only that, but the following month, the long-anticipated city sandbox gacha game Ananta will be launching on January 15, 2027 for PS5, Android, iOS, and PC specifically via Steam, as opposed to Petit Planet and Silver Palace’s places on the Epic Games Store outside of dedicated clients.

It’s also worth a reminder that HoYo, in particular, still has a lot of irons in the fire even with Petit Planet officially poised for launch. The most recent test for its creature battling game, Honkai: Nexus Anima, ran this past summer, while one of its other new brand-new IPs, Nodusfall, was announced at Gamescom back in August, showing a much darker fantasy aesthetic compared to the more anime-based stylings of Genshin, ZZZ, and the Honkai games.

#4485. Our Long-Term 2026 Honda Passport Is Still a Hot Commodity

With its plush interior and a commodious cargo hold, our boxy Honda has become the car-board-lottery jackpot for those planning a road trip.

“I’ve finally won!” exclaims technical editor Austin Irwin in response to snagging our long-term 2026 Honda Passport TrailSport for the weekend. Typically, it’s sports cars, rolling palaces, or vehicles with a manual transmission that elicit that type of reaction during our weekly sign-out process, not mid-size two-row SUVs. But the Passport really does have that effect on folks around here.

While it’s nowhere near the most engaging vehicle at our office at any given time, our sunburnt Honda’s allure comes from its ability to effortlessly eat both cargo and miles in large sums. Depending on your weekend plans, that can be far more valuable than the Hattori Hanzō–sharp steering precision of a 911 or the rewarding snick of a Miata’s six-speed shifter.

In the 10,000 miles since we last checked in, a handful of editors have taken full advantage of the Passport’s strengths. In just a few short months, it checked Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, and Ohio off its regional-visitation checklist, with one sentiment echoed by the three staffers upon returning from their respective excursions: The Passport is a damn good road tripper.

See all results for new 2026 Honda Passport for sale near 94402

“Taking the Passport on a trip through Ohio to Hocking Hills was very enjoyable,” said online production assistant Sarah Taylor, who specifically called out its smooth ride and competent handling on winding mountain roads. Senior social media editor Carter Fry also joined in on praising the Honda’s on-road demeanor, noting that the SUV “is so well balanced considering its size and all-terrain tires.” A plush ride and confidence-inspiring handling are important traits on long-distance trips, but the Passport’s comfortable and expansive interior is what really cements it as our resident road-trip hero.

“Cavernous,” “spacious,” and “generous” have all appeared in the Passport’s in-car logbook to describe its cargo accommodations, and it is indeed very roomy back there by mid-size-SUV standards. In our testing, we managed to stuff under its liftgate 16 carry-on suitcases with the rearmost seats in their upright position and 38 carry-ons with the rear bench folded down. That’s 13 and nine more than will fit in a Toyota 4Runner, respectively. Managing news editor Eric Stafford did his best to stretch the Passport’s people and stuff-hauling capabilities to their limit on a ski trip to northern Wisconsin and reported that there was more than enough room to comfortably accommodate three guys and all their gear. So far, no one has been able to find anything that doesn’t fit in the Passport's cargo hold, but we’ll keep brainstorming.

As far as grievances are concerned, there haven’t been many. Several editors have reported software issues related to phone pairing, Google Maps connectivity, and Apple CarPlay glitches. On one occasion, the infotainment screen went blank but continued to play music from the grave. On another, the GPS display within the digital gauge cluster got confused and gave up despite that Android Auto was running with no connectivity issues. Both of those incidents were resolved with a simple restart. Aside from that, there’s an ambiguous logbook comment likening the Passport’s interior to “something you’d order out of an L.L. Bean catalog,” but it's unclear whether that was meant as a compliment or a dig. Depends on how much you like cable-knit sweaters, we suppose.

See all results for new 2026 Honda Passport for sale near 94402

There isn’t much to report from a service or repair standpoint, either. Since we took in the Passport for its 10,000-mile oil service, which was covered under Honda’s one-year, 12,000-mile complimentary maintenance coverage, the sole out-of-pocket expense we’ve incurred was for the Passport’s 20,000-mile service, which included an oil and filter change, a tire rotation, and an inspection, for a total of $184. The only change to the TrailSport’s hardware was a swap back to its original 275/60R-18 General Grabber A/T Sport tires after the shedding of its Continental VikingContact 8 winters, but we handled that ourselves.

While it’s uncommon for a family SUV to be a first-round pick in an office full of performance-pilled enthusiasts, it’s clear why our long-term Passport is so highly coveted. With its coddling seats, plush but poised ride quality, and seemingly boundless cargo hold, the Passport is a hard act to beat when you’re staring down a thousand-mile road trip. As long as C/D staffers remain adventurous, we’re sure that the Passport’s key fob will continue to be fought over in the 20,000 miles to come.

The first few months of a new job can be stressful, especially when you have more than 20 professional scrutinizers judging you at all times, constantly scheming new ways to push you until your wheels fall off. Some might call that a hostile work environment, but that’s daily life for the vehicles in the Car and Driver long-term test fleet. While some of our long-termers are progressively eased into their 40,000 miles of hard labor, our Honda Passport TrailSport Elite was afforded no such luxury. Soon after it got acquainted with its new handlers, we threw it headfirst into the ultimate utility litmus test as a support vehicle for our most recent Lightning Lap event.

For those unfamiliar with our annual gantlet of speed, here are the CliffsNotes: We round up the newest street-legal performance cars and set course for Virginia International Raceway in Alton, Virginia. Once there, our editors attack the 4.1-mile Grand Course configuration with as much aplomb as they dare, reporting back with lap times and harrowing tales of grit and grandeur from behind the wheel. It is quite the production, and with 16 vehicles in need of attention at this year's event, a capable gear hauler was as important as ever.

We decided that a 12-foot U-Haul box trailer would best suit our needs, so we rented one and loaded it with items crucial for the operation, including jacks, jack stands, scales, test equipment, tires, a grill, and a hot-dog rotisserie. After filling the trailer well short of the Passport's 5000-pound maximum towing capacity, we backed our rig up to its new companion for the 600-plus-mile journey to the Virginia–North Carolina border. Mating the two was easy with the TrailSport Elite's multiview backup camera. Our only gripe was the position of our Passport's hitch receiver, which was a little low for our use case, but we made it work. With the supplies loaded and a full tank of gas, we hit the road.

Road warrior Christi VanSyckle was tasked with piloting our traffic-cone-colored Honda across multiple state lines and the Appalachian Mountains. She arrived at the track with a positive report card for the Passport, saying that “stability was confident at highway speeds through the mountains.” She added that the cabin was surprisingly quiet and the seats provided enough support that she never felt the need to stop and stretch. Gold stars for comfort and capability. Nothing changed on the return trip, so we'd say that the Passport aced its doozy of an initiation test.

Back home, the Passport was finally given the chance to settle into a more mundane daily rhythm. It continued to draw praise as more editors had the chance to slide behind the wheel. In the logbook comments that trickled in, one comparison continued to pop up: "It used to be the Accord sedan, but the V-6 family Honda is now an SUV. I'm surprisingly okay with it," said editor-in-chief Tony Quiroga. That thought was echoed by staff photographer Michael Simari, who mused, "The Passport's Accord-like agreeableness continues to grow on me."

Being likened to the 40-time 10Best-winning Honda Accord is quite the compliment, and the comparison makes a lot of sense considering the Passport shares the Accord's practical, ergonomically satisfying, and well-rounded demeanor. Its softly sprung ride makes long-distance travel comfortable and effortless, and its voluminous rear cabin grants back-seat passengers an especially generous amount of stretch-out space. Up front, the 12.3-inch touchscreen is quick to respond to inputs, and the physical steering-wheel buttons and climate-control toggles are positioned just right. Some drivers have experienced Apple CarPlay connectivity issues, but that is likely due in part to the dozens of phones constantly cycling through our car's system.

While our time with the Passport has been mostly smiles so far, a couple of sore spots have surfaced. The 3.5-liter V-6 under the hood has received mixed reviews, with the main pain point being its lack of low-rpm grunt. Its full 262 pound-feet of peak torque doesn't arrive until 5000 rpm, which, combined with our test vehicle's 4702 pounds, leads to a notable delay in gumption after kicking the go pedal. One comment also mentioned the 10-speed automatic's indifferent attitude toward downshifting, which contributes to the malaise, especially during city driving and highway merging. These gripes have led some staffers to contemplate what the Passport would be like with an alternative powerplant, with video deputy editor Carlos Lago positing that "a hybrid system would make this feel much punchier, à la Grand Highlander Hybrid."

A hybrid powertrain would also work wonders for the Passport's fuel efficiency, which has nonetheless been reasonable thus far. After more than 10,000 miles, we're averaging 19 mpg, which is 1 mpg less than the TrailSport's EPA combined rating yet a decent figure considering it includes the round trip to VIR with a trailer in tow.

A recent swap to Continental VikingContact 8 winter tires, which set us back a little under $930 with installation, also is likely impacting our fuel economy, but with southeastern Michigan doing its best snow-globe impression over the past few months, it's been a welcome switch. The slightly narrower winter rubber—sized 265/60R-18 versus the OE-spec 275/60R-18s—has made drudging through the polar-apocalyptic wasteland easy, providing nearly undefeatable grip on glassy interstates and unplowed side roads. Road warrior Jacob Kurowicki pointed out that the new tires are a double-edged sword, saying, "This thing is too damn capable in the snow on these winter tires. Being a hooligan requires some commitment." While ride quality hasn’t been impacted to any noticeable degree, cabin noise levels certainly have. Managing testing editor Dave Beard isn't a fan of the racket, proclaiming, "These tires are already getting annoying. How soon can we install some BFGoodrich KO3s?"

So far, the Passport has made two trips to the dealer. The first was at around 6200 miles, when a TD02 code was triggered for a supposed over-the-air software update failure. Resetting the system resulted in a fresh S404 (update unavailable) code, for which the dealer had no solution. We're hoping a future software update will resolve the matter. The second stop was for an oil change, tire rotation, and rear differential fluid change at roughly 10,200 miles. Both services were free under Honda's one-year or 12,000-mile complimentary maintenance coverage, and we haven't encountered any other issues that would force us to fork over some dough.

Despite the abhorrent weather, our time with the Passport has been mostly sunny. Even faced with a particularly difficult challenge right out of the gate, our long-termer has proved its worth as a formidable hauler, a practical errand-runner, and a comfortable road-trip companion.

Months in Fleet: 5 months Current Mileage: 10,919 milesAverage Fuel Economy: 19 mpg Fuel Tank Size: 18.5 gal Observed Fuel Range: 350 miles Service: $0 Normal Wear: $0 Repair: $0 Damage and Destruction: $0

Since the Honda Passport was revived for the 2019 model year, it has racked up some significant Car and Driver accolades. Upon its return to the market, the Passport promptly conquered its contemporaries in a five-car two-row mid-size-SUV comparison test. After its strong showing, we invited a 2019 Passport EX-L to live with us for a while, where it proved to be a comfortable, practical, and (mostly) unproblematic companion for 40,000 miles. The Passport has also earned a spot on our Editors' Choice list every year since its revival, and now it has joined the ranks among the industry's best as a 2026 10Best laureate.

While the outgoing generation was certainly deserving of the praise it received, one thing was desperately missing from its arsenal: allure. The Passport had utility mastered, but its anonymous styling and drab interior made it as appetizing as boiled chicken. Honda has addressed that point with the new 2026 Passport, which now looks much more appealing with its brawny, cubist sheetmetal and enhanced capabilities. With it now more flavorful, we're going in for a second serving, inviting the Passport back for another 40,000-mile stress test.

When it came time to spec our new long-termer, we had an important decision to make. While every 2026 Passport comes with all-wheel drive, a 3.5-liter V-6, and a 10-speed automatic transmission, there's a sizable difference between the base RTL and the off-road-focused TrailSport. Plenty of C/D staffers aren't afraid to get dirty, so we decided to pull the trigger on a TrailSport Elite to ensure that no mud pit would go uncrossed.

While the Passport is still not quite as capable as some of the body-on-frame options in the segment, such as the Toyota 4Runner or the Ford Bronco, it's clear that tough-terrain capability was a top priority for the newest Passport. As with all other TrailSport models, our TrailSport Elite comes with plenty of gear to aid in our off-pavement antics, including skid plates that provide genuine underbody protection, an off-road-oriented suspension tune, a torque-vectoring rear axle within the all-wheel-drive system, easy-access recovery points that are rated for twice the Passport's weight, and 18-inch wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires. An integrated trailer hitch rated for 5000 pounds of towing capacity comes standard, as do amber daytime running lights, which are less about function but really add some unique character to the Passport's facia.

While we left the boxes on our long-termer's rather short options list largely unchecked (other than the one for Sunset Orange paint at $455), the TrailSport Elite is jam-packed with its fair share of luxuries as a premium trim in the Passport model hierarchy. Standard features include heated and ventilated leather front seats, a panoramic moonroof, heated side mirrors, a Bose audio system, a power liftgate, puddle lights, a heated leather 60/40-split rear bench seat, and a 12.3-inch infotainment touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Our final tally: $54,355.

Regardless of trim, the Passport is powered by a 285-hp 3.5-liter V-6 mated to a 10-speed automatic transmission. There is no other engine available. While the 2026 Passport's double-overhead-cam V-6 makes five more horsepower than the outgoing generation's 280-hp SOHC 3.5-liter V-6, the new model's additional weight obviates any gains made by the updated powertrain from an acceleration standpoint. The verdict on the Passport's gumption is split, with some noting that it feels quick enough and others musing if it feels underpowered.

Regardless of our subjective opinions, numbers don't lie, and our TrailSport Elite is much slower than the previous-generation Passport. At the test track, our new TrailSport Elite took 7.1 seconds to reach 60 mph—1.2 seconds slower than a 2024 Passport TrailSport that we tested. While a 7.1-second 60-mph time is far from blistering, it's still quicker than a nonhybrid Toyota 4Runner or a nonturbo Subaru Outback.

Lateral grip is one area where the new Passport made significant gains on its predecessor, with our TrailSport Elite circling the skidpad at a respectable 0.84 g compared with 0.74 g for the previous version. Its larger 275/60R-18 General Grabber A/T Sport tires (compared with 245/60R-18 Grabbers on the 2024 TrailSport), in addition to its suspension upgrades and a significantly stiffer chassis, can be mostly credited for the significant increase in grip between generations. Tipping the scales at 4702 pounds, our 2026 rig marginally improved upon its 4237-pound predecessor's braking performance, requiring 177 feet to come to a stop from 70 mph; the 2024 model took 181 feet to stop from the same speed.

The Passport didn't pull off any groundbreaking feats at the track, but its on-road comportment, well-fitted interior, and commodious cargo space have made it a growing favorite among the staff. The TrailSport Elite's muscular new look seems to be a hit—a stark contrast to the last generation, which had as much visual intrigue as a bowl of nonfat Greek yogurt. Several editors have also complimented its comfortable ride and agreeable, if somewhat dull, on-road dynamics. By far the most common praises have been about the Passport's roomy interior and luggage-eating cargo hold, spaces which feel almost geometry-defying within a mid-size-SUV envelope.

After a few months with the Passport, the collective outlook for our sun-kissed Honda is optimistic. As we venture deeper into what is turning out to be a frigid Michigan winter, our Passport will be subjected to grueling Midwest snowstorms, icy roads, and any wintertime shenanigans our editors can dream up. We'll check in again at the 10,000-mile mark to let you know what those shenanigans entail as the miles add up.

#4484. Tesla Powerwall 3 now boosts heat pumps to store cheap solar as heat

Tesla has launched Heat Pump Optimization, a feature that lets the Powerwall 3 and three-phase Powerwall 3P tell a compatible heat pump when to run harder so a home can bank cheap or surplus solar energy as hot water.

It’s live in Europe only. Tesla hasn’t said anything about bringing it to the US or Canada, and the hardware standard it relies on barely exists on this side of the Atlantic.

According to Tesla’s support page for the feature, the Powerwall watches electricity prices and solar production throughout the day and sends the heat pump one of two signals: run normally, or boost.

When it’s told to boost, the heat pump heats water beyond what the home needs right now, typically into a domestic hot water or buffer tank. That stored heat then carries the house through the expensive hours, when the heat pump can run less.

What triggers a boost depends on the Powerwall’s operating mode:

Tesla Energy summed it up on X last week: “Heat Pump Optimization allows your Powerwall to boost heating when there’s surplus solar or energy is inexpensive.”

There’s no cloud integration with heat pump brands here. It’s a wire.

The feature runs on SG-Ready (Smart Grid Ready), a label the German Heat Pump Association (BWP) introduced back in 2012 with 17 manufacturers. It uses two relay contacts on the heat pump to signal four operating states, from a utility block to a forced switch-on. Tesla only uses the “normal” and “boosted” recommendations.

Tesla’s requirements are pretty specific:

And there are limits. The signals are only recommendations, so the heat pump’s own thermostat settings can override them. Tesla also notes each signal has to be held for at least 10 minutes to comply with SG-Ready, and the feature drops back to normal during a power outage so the Powerwall can prioritize backup loads.

Oddly, there’s no on/off toggle in the Tesla app. Once it’s wired up, it’s on.

The math is what makes this interesting. A 300-liter hot water tank heated an extra 30°C holds about 10.5 kWh of thermal energy. With a heat pump running at a COP of 3, that takes only around 3.5 kWh of electricity to store.

So a tank most European heat pump homes already have can soak up a big chunk of midday solar without touching the lithium in the garage. That leaves the Powerwall’s 13.5 kWh free for the stuff that can’t be stored as heat.

The market is there too. Germany sold 299,000 heating heat pumps in 2025, up 55% year-over-year according to BWP, and they made up nearly half of all new heating systems sold in the country for the first time.

Tesla is also late to this. sonnen pushed a software update in 2023 that lets its sonnenBatterie run heat pumps off surplus solar, starting with NIBE units, and SG-Ready control has been a standard feature of German PV energy managers for years.

watches electricity prices and solar production throughout the day and sends the heat pump one of two signals: run normally, or boost.

Heatpumps over here have been able to do this for years already.

And it's not one of two signals. Inverter controlled HP's enables control of the effect, and not just "normal or boost".

It’s the latest Europe-first move for Tesla Energy after it launched the Powerwall 3P with a native three-phase inverter earlier this year, aimed squarely at Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. The company announced its 1 millionth Powerwall last year, and software like this is how it squeezes more value out of that installed base.

This is a smart, cheap feature, and it’s exactly the kind of thing that makes a home battery more valuable without adding a single cell.

Heat is the biggest energy load in most homes in cold climates, and water is about the cheapest storage medium there is. Using a battery’s brain to time the heat pump around solar and tariffs makes a lot more sense than discharging lithium to run a compressor at 6 p.m.

Home batteries are changing the economics of residential energy, and pairing them with solar (and smart loads like heat pumps) is the best way to get the most out of them. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. The Best-Selling Hyundai SUV In October Wasn’t The Tucson

We want you to imagine a Rolls-Royce owner. If you pictured someone a little bit older, then we can’t blame you. The name conjures images of old-world luxury with massive estates and links to royalty. It’s either that or said owner is a captain of industry, being whisked away to important social gatherings across cities.

But while the automaker still offers traditional luxury in spades, it’s also managed to lower the average age of its buyers. As it turns out, classic luxury cars have a strong appeal for younger, affluent shoppers. The thing is, Rolls-Royce didn’t just become a brand that suddenly attracted a new era of customers, but rather, it made the effort to make it happen.

Julian Jenkins is the director of sales and brand for Rolls-Royce, and he recently told Automotive News that the average customer is 43 years old. You read that right; it’s older millennials who are now buying these cars. Before 2010, the average age was 56 years old, so how did the brand do it?

He added that, in some markets, the brand is showing relevance among the ultra-wealthy Gen-Z crowd. “In China, for example, we have some of our youngest clients who are in their mid to late 20s,” said Jenkins. There’s no doubt that China played a part in making Rolls-Royce a ‘young’ brand.

Jenkins pointed out that the Cullinan played a key role in bringing in younger customers to the marque, but it’s not the only reason for the drop in average ages. “Black Badge, Cullinan and also some of our bespoke creations have done that,” Jenkins said, further adding that it’s the ultra-exclusive Coachbuild division models such as the Boat Tail and Droptail actually attracting a younger crowd. “Those are Rolls-Royce models that have stimulated interest,” added the executive.

Rolls-Royce has since responded to the new wave of customers by transforming its showrooms. Case in point, Rolls-Royce Motor Cars Beverly Hills went from merely selling cars to a place that hosts gatherings with its speakeasy-inspired lounge and bar. It’s called the Black Badge Lounge, and before anyone dismisses it as a gimmick, it’s actually become a destination for current and prospective owners. The showroom overhaul gives the client a more immersive experience.

Rival Bentley has also adapted a similar approach when it unveiled its new look for its shops. Jack Barclay Bentley in London was the first to get the boutique treatment, and like Rolls-Royce Beverly Hills, a large part of the store is dedicated as a bar that doubles as the reception area. As for Mercedes, it’s building standalone stores for the Maybach division to provide an exclusive and unique experience that’s far elevated from the usual Mercedes-Benz showroom. The aim is to make the visit feel less transactional and more warm and welcoming.

Also, Milton Pedraza, CEO of Luxury Institute, mentioned that the baby boomers who once made up a big chunk of Rolls-Royce sales are gradually fading out. Instead of simply sticking firmly to tradition, the British automaker managed to infuse its values while tailoring it to a new generation of customers. “Rolls-Royce truly is an iconic brand. It’s one of those like Hermes: It’s been around for generations and it continues to reinvent itself. Now reinventing itself into more bespoke. You pay half a million for the base and then you spend another half a million on ‘Customize it for me,'” said Pedraza.

Of course, the brand’s customers have always wanted a more bespoke vehicle, so it’s not a generational thing. The difference now is, it’s tweaked the formula and moved with the times.

#4482. Cadillac’s most affordable EV just got a bit cheaper

The 2027 Cadillac Optiq offers up to 317 miles of range, a massive 33″ infotainment screen, an NACS charge port, and now it’s a bit more affordable.

The Optiq first went on sale in 2025 as Cadillac’s entry-level electric SUV, starting at $54,390. For the 2026 model year, the Optiq arrived as GM’s first electric vehicle with a built-in NACS port and added a new rear-wheel-drive (RWD) powertrain.

Thanks to the new RWD option, the 2026 Optiq (see our review) was also slightly less expensive, with prices starting at $52,395.

While GM initially said the 2027 Cadillac Optiq would start at $52,695, prices on its website have been updated and are now slightly lower.

The base 2027 Cadillac Optiq Luxury RWD is now listed at $51,790, or $905 less than the initial price announced months ago. The Luxury AWD trim is also $905 cheaper, starting at $55,290.

Meanwhile, the Sport trim now starts at $52,395 for RWD and $55,895 for AWD, both $900 less than before.

The higher-spec Optiq Premium Luxury, Premium Sport, and V-Series trims remain at the price GM initially announced.

The 2027 Cadillac Optiq offers up to 317 miles of range in the RWD models and 303 miles with AWD. All models come with a standard 33″ Horizon Display infotainment screen, a 19-speaker AKG Studio Audio System, GM’s Super Cruise hands-free driver-assist technology, and a native NACS charge port.

Upgrading to AWD costs an extra $3,500. The Premium Luxury and Premium Sport add standard features including a Head-Up Display, ventilated and lumbar massaging front seats, and a rear cargo cover.

The high-performance 2027 Optiq-V starts at $69,295 and delivers a Cadillac-estimated 519 lb-ft of torque and 650 horsepower in Velocity MaX Mode,

How does the Cadillac Optiq stack up against the Tesla Model Y? The base Tesla Model Y RWD starts at $39,990 with up to 321 miles of range, while the AWD version costs $41,990 and gets up to 294 miles.

The Tesla Model Y Premium RWD starts at $45,990 with up to 355 miles of range, while the Premium AWD starts at $49,990 and has 327 miles of range.

Had the opportunity to drive the Optiq as a loaner while my Lyriq was in for service. I truly liked how it handled but I did find what I call a safety issue due to its design. The A pillar has an extra vertical piece and that combined with really no usable visual space forward and the side mirror create a blind spot when wanting to make a left turn on dark roads. No problem in the city where there is light. If GM would have added front side lighting when making a turn that could have been eliminated. Would have seriously looked at the Optiq for the next vehicle but that blind spot is a show stopper for me. Well that, and the fact the Optiq does not support CarPlay.

Inside, the base Tesla Model Y has a 16″ QHD touchscreen and 7-speaker audio system. The Premium model gains a 15-speaker Tesla Audio System with a subwoofer, plus an 8″ second-row touchscreen.

The two are nearly the same size, but the Tesla Model Y offers slightly more rear legroom and cargo capacity than the Cadillac Optiq.
